channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal trade cuts trees and sustains households
item.description: A burner says his family relies on the work, while the environmental agency warns that cutting economic trees threatens food security.

item.title: Sierra Leone's electricity and water regulator lifts revenue to NLE 7.4 million
item.description: The regulator, which licenses power and water firms, collected NLE 7.4 million from levies and licenses in 2024, up from NLE 2.3 million in 2023.

item.title: Sierra Leone's vice presidency has rarely led to the presidency
item.description: A political analyst argues that the office has often served party balancing rather than preparing its holders to succeed the president.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea Senate president proposes rules for traditional marriage
item.description: Teresa Efua Asangono says wedding expenses are delaying formal unions and pushing many couples into cohabitation.

item.title: Tanzania splits foreign affairs ministry into two
item.description: President Samia Suluhu Hassan appointed Angellah Kairuki to lead East African Cooperation and kept Mahmoud Thabit Kombo in charge of foreign affairs.

item.title: Praia raises annual grants for three music groups to 750,000 escudos
item.description: The municipality raised Ferro Gaita's grant from 500,000 escudos and extended the same annual support to Bulimundo and Os Tubarões.

item.title: Kiir ends emergency rule in four South Sudan states
item.description: The order restores ordinary duties to state and national institutions, while an analyst says the emergency failed to stop violence.

item.title: Namibian police begin training 1 980 new cadets
item.description: The recruits started on 1 November at three training centres after 2 050 cadet constables graduated in May and June.

item.title: PETROSOL Platinum Energy wins Oil and Gas Company of the Year award in Ghana
item.description: The Ghanaian-owned oil marketer received the honour at the 6th Chamber Business Awards for its performance in the 2025 business year.

item.title: Somalia to start issuing EAC e-passport in January, ahead of South Sudan
item.description: Somalia will become the latest East African Community partner state to issue the regional travel document, and South Sudan has yet to begin.

item.title: Benin plans a learning city in each of its six development hubs
item.description: Decentralisation Minister Janvier Yahouédéhou presented the plan in Cotonou and cited Porto-Novo, admitted to UNESCO's learning-cities network in 2025, as the model.

item.title: South Sudan adviser says civil servants work unpaid for months or years
item.description: Joseph Ngere Paciko said workers continue to report for duty and cover daily expenses themselves despite prolonged salary delays.

item.title: Fashola says Tinubu's identity questions resurface before elections
item.description: The former Lagos governor says Tinubu met the constitutional requirements to contest and predicts he will win again in 2027.

item.title: Dakar court sets 9 December ruling on CFA200 million claim
item.description: Mame Mbaye Niang wants the transfer of a 250-square-metre Keur Gorgui villa annulled so he can pursue the damages awarded against Ousmane Sonko.

item.title: Zambia’s Constitutional Court to rule on Bill 7 petition
item.description: The LCK Freedom Foundation argues that Parliament breached constitutional procedure when it passed the 2025 amendment law.

item.title: MTC commits N$135.6 million to sponsorships and social investment over three years
item.description: The telecoms operator says its cumulative contribution to sponsorships and corporate social investment now stands at about N$420 million.

item.title: Mozambique launches fashion council and sector mapping
item.description: The new council plans to map professionals, businesses and institutions as Maputo hosts a forum and fashion week from 7 to 12 December.

item.title: Tanzania seeks Siemens Energy partnership for gas-fired power projects
item.description: Talks in Sweden covered private investment, financing and technology transfer as Tanzania looks to expand electricity generation.

item.title: Maersk plans full Suez Canal service return by March 2027
item.description: The carrier has resumed canal and Red Sea operations, while its CEO says the rest of its network will return over coming months.

item.title: Libya agrees visit to assess border surveillance towers
item.description: The Customs Authority and the European Union mission will inspect sites near Tunisia and discuss repairs, equipment and a proposed joint monitoring centre.

item.title: Burkina Faso’s zinc mine resumes operations under state subsidiary
item.description: The mine had been shut since 2022 floods that killed eight people; the transition president is due to attend its restart.

item.title: Ivory Coast suspends influencer’s driving licence for four years
item.description: The influencer admitted speeding at 120 km/h on a road limited to 100 km/h, and must return to driving school before regaining his licence.

item.title: Bank of Zambia to explain latest monetary policy rate decision
item.description: The central bank is presenting its latest rate decision and the reasons behind it at a live briefing.

item.title: DR Congo assembly takes up two electoral reform bills
item.description: Lawmakers are examining proposals to reform the electoral commission and the electoral law as the September session nears its close.

item.title: ESCOM prepares mass disconnections over K77 billion in unpaid bills
item.description: Government ministries and agencies account for more than half of the power utility’s approximately K77 billion debt, officials told Parliament.

item.title: Guinea-Bissau delays presidential and parliamentary elections until 2028
item.description: A decree moves the vote from 6 December to 26 November 2028 after the presidency said election preparations lacked sufficient resources.

item.title: Trafigura names Helio Cumbi to lead Mozambique operations
item.description: The Mozambican executive will oversee the company’s energy, metals and minerals activities in the country and oil-business development across eastern and southern Africa.

item.title: Oulampane mayor remains in serious condition after suspected arson
item.description: Sagar Coly was burned at his home in Diacounda on Thursday and transferred to Ziguinchor for specialised treatment.

item.title: Malawi blocks film premiere at Lilongwe convention centre
item.description: The government cited the censorship law, while the production company says the film had been submitted for review on November 23.

item.title: Guinea raises monthly sanitation budget for Conakry communes to 15 billion francs
item.description: The minister puts the real monthly cost at 23 billion francs for Conakry and 109 billion nationwide, against the old 3 billion to 3.5 billion.

item.title: Engage Salone finds Sierra Leone councils score 29.8 out of 100
item.description: A survey of 1,489 people across six council areas found 60% said their council never consults communities.

item.title: Chad's justice ministry orders prosecutors to stop police custody in civil disputes
item.description: A 25 November circular tells prosecutors general to summon judicial police officers and enforce the ban on custody in civil, commercial and social cases.

item.title: Bolgatanga and Nalerigu to hit 39°C as storms loom in the south
item.description: Localised afternoon and evening thunderstorms are forecast for coastal and inland southern areas after a misty start.

item.title: Mauritius charges two former deputy governors over MIC hiring
item.description: The former officials are accused of favouring a CEO candidate; one also faces a charge over raising his monthly salary without board approval.

item.title: MPEC seeks to unseat ruling party in Dja and Lobo’s five seats
item.description: Professor Jean-Calvin Aba’a Oyono leads a six-person slate challenging the ruling party’s hold on the department’s National Assembly seats.

item.title: Nigerian student wins bronze at Riyadh innovation contest
item.description: Rimas Mohamed earned the medal for an environmental sustainability project at a competition that brought together teams from 55 countries.

item.title: West Darfur launches campaign to protect women and girls from violence
item.description: The state began its 16 Days of Activism drive as officials and aid workers warned that war and displacement heighten risks of abuse.

item.title: Boakai ties Liberia’s US$5.7 billion infrastructure plan to future gold revenue
item.description: The agreement with Bea Mountain Mining Corporation covers four power plants, a transmission network and 14 road and bridge projects over five years.

item.title: Togo opposition groups meet in Brussels to discuss coordination
item.description: Organisers say the 27-29 November gathering will seek new political directions and a permanent forum for joint decisions and resolving disputes.

item.title: Uganda wildlife board to review tourism revenue-sharing
item.description: Chairman James Kalema says the board will assess whether communities near protected areas benefit effectively from tourism income.

item.title: Chad declares 28 November a public holiday
item.description: The government says the holiday for the Republic’s proclamation covers public and private workers nationwide, with work resuming on Monday, 30 November.

item.title: Liberia’s petroleum regulator sets 2027 deadline for first sector report
item.description: The five-year plan also follows the authority’s report of US$13.8 million in contributions to the national budget over three years.

item.title: Liberia's Senate orders probe into cash shortage and high prices
item.description: The inquiry follows complaints that banknotes remain scarce and essential goods costly despite the local currency's appreciation to about L$163 per US$1.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea vice-president seeks stricter Miss selection rules
item.description: Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue says candidates at home and abroad should have equal opportunities while demonstrating knowledge of the country.

item.title: Liberia's agriculture minister warns El Niño could cut rice yields by up to 50%
item.description: Dr. J. Alexander Nuetah told lawmakers severe conditions could reduce yields by 30 to 50% for crops planted during the affected period.

item.title: Tanzania secures US$85 million for maternal and newborn care
item.description: The five-year Beginnings Fund partnership will support 210 mainland facilities and allocate US$9.6 million to Zanzibar.

item.title: Algeria issues orange rain alerts for 22 wilayas
item.description: The meteorological office forecasts 20 to 40 mm in some areas, after farmers raised concern over a lack of rain during ploughing.

item.title: Ebola infects 29 MSF response team members in DR Congo
item.description: Three members of the teams have died since the country’s 17th Ebola epidemic began, according to Actualite.cd.

item.title: Mauritius opens talks on 2027 wage compensation
item.description: Unions seek between Rs 1 200 and Rs 1 700, while employers urge restraint ahead of a government decision expected in December.

item.title: Kalumbila officer urges Kakaindu residents to form companies
item.description: District officer Frank Siatwinda says residents should position themselves to compete for business opportunities and contracts from local mining companies.

item.title: Zimbabwe's state power utility cuts Harare power for eight and a half hours
item.description: The utility says customers served by its Kuwadzana and Glen View centres will be affected across more than 30 suburbs and farming areas.

item.title: DStv unveils five lower-priced packages in Botswana
item.description: The redesign, its first in 30 years, adds dedicated sports and film options, and the Starter package now offers more than 85 channels.

item.title: Mauritius opens inquiry after inmate found dead at Melrose prison
item.description: The 52-year-old was found on his bed on 25 November, and drugs were later found under the bed and on partly burned paper.

item.title: Mauritius schedules five National Super League matches
item.description: The fourth round of the 2026-2027 season opens Friday at St François Xavier stadium and ends Monday evening.

item.title: Oyedele urges Nigerian firms to compete under AfCFTA
item.description: The finance minister says access to African markets will bring prosperity only if businesses produce competitively and diversify exports.

item.title: Attaf denies Algeria ordered a boycott of French goods
item.description: The foreign minister said French suppliers lost ground on price and competition, and urged Paris to use the EU-Algeria Association Council to discuss the dispute.

item.title: Lilayi fire victim appeals to well-wishers for help after losing home
item.description: Bumba Hilusenga lost her property when a fire gutted her home in early November 2026, and she is now asking for assistance from the public.

item.title: Visa opens Kampala office as Uganda's central bank demands cheaper payments
item.description: Governor Michael Atingi-Ego also urged the company to help lenders assess small firms and strengthen protection against rising cybercrime.

item.title: Mozambique parliament approves 2025 State Account over opposition objections
item.description: Frelimo used its parliamentary majority to pass the resolution as all three opposition parties voted against it, alleging unlawful public spending.

item.title: Guinea's labour minister takes lead of African labour administration centre
item.description: Ramatoulaye Camara was elected board president for one year at the 45th ordinary session in Conakry, while another Guinean official was named to head the centre for three years.

item.title: Mozambique’s 100 largest companies record 615 billion meticais in turnover
item.description: President Daniel Chapo announced the 2025 figure and called for reforms to improve the business environment.

item.title: FNB Namibia warns digital banking growth is changing fraud risks
item.description: Digital channels now carry most of the bank's transactions, and criminals are using artificial intelligence to make impersonation harder to spot.

item.title: Mali’s kidney congress highlights gaps in specialist care and prevention
item.description: The meeting cited five dialysis centres but said the country lacks operational peritoneal dialysis and kidney-transplant services.

item.title: Moody’s keeps Mauritius outlook negative, says upgrade unlikely soon
item.description: The agency wants sustained evidence of lower public debt and improved state finances before it considers stabilising its view.

item.title: Tunisia closes Jebel Jelloud road for two nights of south-entry works
item.description: The Ministry of Equipment and Housing says a section of national road 1 (RN1) will shut from 22:00 to 05:00 on 27 and 28 November, with detours for both directions.

item.title: Madagascar targets 5.1% growth in 2027 budget
item.description: The plan raises public spending by 11% and relies on higher tax and customs receipts to finance 24 priority programmes.

item.title: EU-backed programme mobilises €52.3 million for 396 Tunisian businesses
item.description: The €170 million Tunisia Economic Recovery programme has reached companies in 23 governorates, with financing still open to applicants.

item.title: Burkina Faso hosts China-focused forum on cultural and human exchange
item.description: The 26-27 November gathering at the University of Burkina brings together students, Chinese diplomats, experts and businesspeople, alongside participants from Gabon, Cameroon.

item.title: El Chanel to perform in N'Djamena on 30 November to promote « Nagada »
item.description: The Cameroonian singer's 10-track album, released on 31 October, deals with love, social realities and gratitude to God.

item.title: African Development Bank warns of hidden PPP costs to Central African finances
item.description: The bank says infrastructure deals carry real future payment commitments whose cost remains largely outside public accounts.

item.title: Ruto and Mnangagwa open presidential commission on Kenya-Zimbabwe ties
item.description: The leaders are due to review existing agreements and trade barriers, with Kenya targeting US$70 million in annual bilateral trade.

item.title: Primus Ligue schedules Vital’O-Flambeau du Centre opener
item.description: The 14th-round match is set for Friday at 15:00 at Urunani, with three more fixtures scheduled for Saturday.

item.title: Uganda's Dei BioPharma says it is ready to supply Africa's medicine market
item.description: Founder Matthias Magoola says the company has more than 500 products and will launch six antimalarial medicines within two weeks.

item.title: Powered by Africa plans $100 million real estate fund for diaspora investors
item.description: The platform launched in Accra after a five-day gathering that drew delegates from 27 African countries and beyond.

item.title: Malawi's doctors' union calls for health-sector emergency
item.description: Shortages of medicines, fuel and staff have left public hospitals unable to deliver essential care, the union says.

item.title: Italy's embassy takes MOZITA Jazz Festival to Beira and Pemba
item.description: The festival's second edition runs from 3 to 8 December 2026, extending its Italy-Mozambique musical exchange beyond Maputo.

item.title: Moyen-Chari trains more than 50 women to protect children's rights
item.description: The provincial delegation for women and early childhood, with UNICEF support, is addressing child marriage and female genital mutilation in Sarh.

item.title: Malawi’s black-market dollar reaches K5,000 as official rate holds at K1,751
item.description: Spot checks in major cities found vendors buying dollars for K4,500 to K4,700 and selling them for K5,000.

item.title: South Africa braces for storms before a drier El Niño summer
item.description: Forecasters say thunderstorms are due over the Free State and Gauteng, and temperatures will climb to 32ºC-36ºC once the cloud over the interior clears.

item.title: Oceana reports 29% fall in Namibia horse mackerel catch
item.description: Vessel surveys and late-year quota shortages cut fishing time, while average Rand selling prices climbed 18%.

item.title: Burundi releases cameraman after days in intelligence-service detention
item.description: Bonaventure Niyongabo left custody on Thursday evening after the national intelligence service gave no public reason for holding him.

item.title: Bank Windhoek raises N$650 million through JSE note sale
item.description: The three-year unsecured notes drew more than N$3.3 billion in bids and were priced 0.66 percentage points tighter than the bank’s previous bond listing.

item.title: Burundi transfers four Mpimba figures to three prisons
item.description: The former director and two officials are accused of granting businessperson Aloys Ntakarutimana privileges during his detention at Mpimba.

item.title: Abiy says Eritrea rejected power, road and port offers as tensions grow
item.description: Ethiopia's prime minister accuses Asmara of arming forces hostile to Ethiopia and warns that destruction will fall upon Eritrea if it does not change course.

item.title: Burundi trafficking networks use five routes to send children to Tanzania
item.description: An advocacy group says the routes cross several provinces and urges the government to strengthen enforcement and revise the 2014 trafficking law.

item.title: Cholera infects 12 Saint-Marc pupils as Bujumbura water shortage persists
item.description: Seven pupils were taken to hospital Wednesday and five more Thursday; the boarding school has reportedly lacked drinking water for nearly two weeks.

item.title: Uganda and SANY Group agree to develop green investment proposals
item.description: The proposed work covers urban sanitation, recycling infrastructure and electric trucks, but the meeting produced no funding commitment or project timetable.

item.title: Terkper urges Ghana to resist fresh borrowing after debt defaults
item.description: The former finance minister says the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) initiative, later defaults and the domestic debt exchange should keep successive governments.

item.title: Togo's bishops raise alarm over missing priest in Kara
item.description: The Catholic Church says it fears for Father Éric Ébélaki, a parish vicar who has not been heard from since 24 November.

item.title: Edenia takes Malagasy chocolate to Paris-area Christmas fair
item.description: The Madagascar craft chocolatier plans to show about 15 products at the 19 December event organised by ASASOA France-Madagascar.

item.title: Madagascar’s armed forces receive 12 drones and qualify 17 military personnel
item.description: The two-week course included 70 flight hours, with the armed forces expected to train future pilots independently.

item.title: Nigeria's agency and AGRA target $25m for farm-business financing
item.description: AGRA has committed an initial $100,000 to a facility meant to make professional business support more affordable for agribusinesses.

item.title: Mali approves state transport and logistics company
item.description: The National Transition Council ratified the law establishing the SMTL, which is tasked with freight, passenger transport and logistics facilities.

item.title: Eswatini Cabinet backs judicial inquiry into corruption
item.description: Finance minister Neal Rijkenberg said estimated monthly losses to corruption have risen from E80 million to E90 million.

item.title: Ivory Coast foundation gives schools and clinics to 14 localities
item.description: The national lottery foundation handed over the facilities in Abidjan on Wednesday, with investment of more than CFA456 million across nine regions and districts.

item.title: Ghana's iron and steel corporation plans regulations for Parliament within three months
item.description: The proposed legislative instrument would cover mining, steel processing plants and the scrap metal trade, and the corporation says consultations are in their final stages.

item.title: Senegal's PUMA invests CFA560 million in Casamance schools
item.description: The new facilities are for pupils in villages where displaced families have returned, and form the programme's first phase of support.

item.title: Sierra Leone assigns 28,838 personnel to December census
item.description: Statistics Sierra Leone says the nationwide count starts Dec. 1, after 30,085 applicants sat the final recruitment examination.

item.title: Tunisia detains five suspects in Grand Tunis counterfeit-money case
item.description: Police seized an alleged counterfeiting printer, scanner and banknotes as a sixth suspect became subject to an arrest warrant.

item.title: Mauritania starts 407 million-ouguiya upgrade of Boghé model farm
item.description: The project, financed by the International Development Association and the World Bank Group, will rehabilitate infrastructure and introduce modern irrigation.
